inherits_note: Parent SCN-queens-garden is a container node with no card; garden stone, gravel and box are repeated by value from SCN-rose-tree-yard so the garden stays one look
form: A large oblong croquet lawn enclosed by tall clipped yew hedges, its whole surface heaved into long parallel ridges and furrows; a stone terrace with a balustrade and steps along one long side for the royal party, and a great cedar of Lebanon at one corner casting the shade where guests rest
culture_ref: geography.json#LOC-croquet-lawn; world.json#wonderland_real_counterparts cp-court; culture.json CUL-013, CUL-016, CUL-017
period: Dream-image of the fashionable 1860s croquet party on a college or great-house lawn, the lawn itself replaced by old ridge-and-furrow pasture

grows_from.waking_detail: the fashionable 1860s croquet party of the grown-up world
grows_from.design_growth: A grown-ups' croquet lawn, the smoothest ground a child knows, laid over the ridge-and-furrow of the old ploughland pastures around the family's meadow (the humps every Oxfordshire field walk crosses). The adult game's order and the country's rough ground collide, so the lawn is immaculate close-mown grass that is impossible to play on

dream_design_language: Formal frame, unplayable floor: clipped yew walls, a stone terrace and a cedar frame the ground, while the lawn inside rolls in regular waves like a ploughed field under a green cloth; the ridges read as the long flowing parallel lines of an Art Nouveau panel. The court's colours (red, white, black) appear only in costumes, the striped stakes and the terrace hangings

mucha_design_language.item: Mucha / Art Nouveau: terrace balustrade of carved limestone balusters swelling like lily stems, linked by a frieze of carved roses and vine; the arched hedge openings trimmed in smooth horseshoe curves with wrought-iron whiplash gates (open); a carved circular halo roundel of stone set in the terrace wall behind the royal chairs; gilded wrought-iron awning frame; the green-and-gold iron bench under the cedar in organic scrolls; pastel-and-gold palette over the deep greens
mucha_design_language.culture_ref: world.json#WR-010 (Queen's garden and croquet-ground listed); cultivation.json#XA-magic-08; SCN-rose-tree-yard mucha_design_language
mucha_design_language.why: Same garden language as SCN-rose-tree-yard, realised in built stone, iron and clipped planting

structure.item: an oblong lawn about 60 m by 35 m, close-mown
structure.why: Room for a crowd playing all at once, the procession and the Cat-dispute crowd

structure.item: the whole lawn heaved into parallel ridges and furrows running the length of the ground: crests about 6 m apart, about 60 cm from furrow bottom to crest, smoothly rounded
structure.note: 'it was all ridges and furrows'; dimensions from real medieval ridge-and-furrow, inferred, culture_ref geography.json#LOC-neighbouring-farm

structure.item: tall clipped yew hedges about 3 m high enclosing the ground on three sides, with arched openings cut through at the corners
structure.why: Formal enclosure of a great-house lawn; the openings give exits for arrests and for the walk toward the Gryphon

structure.item: a raised honey-limestone terrace along the fourth long side, about 1 m above the lawn, with a balustrade and a central flight of steps down to the ground; the procession files in along it
structure.note: Alice walking by the White Rabbit as the procession arrives; terrace inferred as the procession route and the King and Queen's vantage

structure.item: a great cedar of Lebanon at one corner of the ground, its flat layered branches making a deep pool of shade on the grass
structure.note: 'resting in the shade'; cedar inferred as the classic Oxford college lawn tree

structure.item: open ground at the lawn's far edge where the crowd gathers round the Cat's head

materials.item: close-mown deep green lawn grass with light and dark mowing stripes following the ridges
materials.why: 'close-cropped lawn grass'; the stripes make the ridges read in wide shots

materials.item: honey-coloured oolitic limestone terrace, balustrade and steps, lichened (same stone as SCN-rose-tree-yard)
cedar of Lebanon: blue-green flat foliage plates, ridged grey-brown trunk

details.item: two wooden croquet winning-stakes at the ends of the ground, painted in rings of red, white and black
details.why: The only period croquet hardware on the ground; the arches are the bent-over soldiers (ch008-p41), so there are no wire hoops

details.item: no hoops set in the lawn; arches are formed by bent-double card-soldier performers
crimson canvas awning over the centre of the terrace with two gilt chairs for the King and Queen
details.why: 1860s croquet parties set seating on the terrace; gives the Queen a place to stamp from

details.item: a cast-iron garden bench under the cedar, painted dark green with gilt highlights, its back a flowing whiplash of lily stems and leaves
details.why: Where guests rest in the shade; the dream's Art Nouveau ironwork

details.item: the live flamingo mallets and hedgehog balls are photoreal CGI animals (proposal, pending_H2): no hoop or ball hardware is built; ground contact marks only
details.note: BIB-0027 extends the photoreal-animal register to non-speaking dream animals (cultivation.json#SUP-002), flagged for H2; SUP-011: no animal ever shown being struck

scale_notes.rule: True 1:1 throughout (Alice 135 cm). No size change is written in ch008-ch009. The ridges are real built earthwork under turf so players stumble for real; the furrow depth (60 cm) must hide a crouching performer's legs, not whole bodies

negative: no flat billiard-table lawn; the ground must visibly roll in ridges and furrows
no modern croquet hoops, no plastic or coloured modern balls
no hedgehog or flamingo ever shown being struck (SUP-011); no cartoon animals; flamingoes and hedgehogs are photoreal CGI animals (pending_H2)
no castle battlements, no fantasy palace in the background
no flat poster illustration, outline graphics or matte-painting finish; photographed built garden
no marquee tents of later style, no bunting, no deck chairs
no playing-card graphics painted on the lawn
prompt_ready_en: a large 1860s English croquet lawn enclosed by tall clipped dark yew hedges, the close-mown green grass heaved into long regular parallel ridges and furrows, a raised honey-coloured limestone terrace with an Art Nouveau balustrade of lily-stem balusters and a carved rose-and-vine frieze, central steps, a crimson awning on a gilded wrought-iron frame over two gilt chairs before a carved stone halo roundel, horseshoe-arched openings in the yew with whiplash iron gates, a great cedar of Lebanon casting deep shade at one corner with a green-and-gold cast-iron bench of flowing lily stems beneath it, red white and black striped croquet stakes at each end, Mucha-inspired pastel-and-gold accents, photographed live-action set
